Definition: a goblet; by analogy, the calyx of a flower
BiblicalUsage: gᵉbîyaʻ means cup, bowl. It occurs 11 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Genesis, Exodus, and Jeremiah — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: What gᵉbîyaʻ tells me is that God speaks plainly, and plain words carry real weight. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
